translationRepairs: In the fifth month, on jichou, he seized Sizhou, paid homage at the ancestral tombs, and offered his father’s spirit an old ox and wine.
In the fifth month, on jichou, he seized Sizhou, paid homage at the ancestral tombs, and bestowed oxen and wine on the local elders.
s0157 賜父老牛酒 means he bestowed oxen and wine on the elders (父老); the original misreads 父老 as an offering to his father’s spirit and attaches 老 to 牛.
In the fifth month, on the jichou day, he took Sizhou, visited the imperial tombs, and bestowed an old ox and wine on his father.
In the fifth month, on the jichou day, he took Sizhou, visited the imperial tombs, and bestowed oxen and wine on the elders.
父老 is the fixed compound for local elders, not ‘his father’; 牛酒 is oxen and wine as a gift, so the literal’s ‘old ox … on his father’ is wrong.
On yichou he came to Jinchuan Gate. The Prince of Gu, Zhu Yunyi, Li Jinglong, and others opened the gates and let him in. The capital fell that day.
On yichou he came to Jinchuan Gate. The Prince of Gu, Zhu Hui, Li Jinglong, and others opened the gates and let him in. The capital fell that day.
s0172 names 谷王橞; 橞 is Hui (Zhu Hui). Zhu Yunyi is not supported by the Chinese personal name.
On the yichou day, he reached Jinchuan Gate; the Prince of Gu Zhu Yunyi, Li Jinglong, and others opened the gate and admitted the Prince; the capital city then fell.
On the yichou day, he reached Jinchuan Gate; the Prince of Gu Zhu Hui, Li Jinglong, and others opened the gate and admitted the Prince; the capital city then fell.
The literal must render 橞 as Hui; Yunyi invents a different given name not present in 谷王橞.
On renshen the Prince of Gu, Zhu Yunyi, was moved to a new fief at Changsha.
On renshen the Prince of Gu, Zhu Hui, was moved to a new fief at Changsha.
s0208 again has 谷王橞; the personal name is Hui, so Zhu Yunyi must be corrected to Zhu Hui.
On the renshen day, the Prince of Gu Zhu Yunyi was transferred in enfeoffment to Changsha.
On the renshen day, the Prince of Gu Zhu Hui was transferred in enfeoffment to Changsha.
Literal 谷王橞 requires Zhu Hui; Yunyi is an English mistranslation of the same given name 橞.
